per_file_findings.issue: The sku and warehouse arguments of fetch() are interpolated directly into the SQL string with an f-string, so a value containing a quote can change the query. fetch_many() passes its skus straight through to this path. Callers are outside this file, so reachability from request input is for the integration pass to confirm.
per_file_findings.suggested_fix: cursor.execute("SELECT qty FROM stock WHERE sku = %s AND warehouse = %s", (sku, warehouse))  # use the placeholder style of the DB driver (%s for psycopg, ? for sqlite3)

per_file_findings.issue: total_qty starts the loop at index 1, so items[0].qty is never added. The docstring says it sums the qty of every item, so any call with two or more items returns a total that is too low by the first item's qty. This affects every caller on common input.
per_file_findings.suggested_fix: for i in range(len(items)): total += items[i].qty, or more simply total = sum(i.qty for i in items)

integration_findings.detected_pattern: api.get_stock(sku) called with one argument after signature change to get_stock(sku, warehouse)
integration_findings.issue: PR 418 added a required warehouse parameter to api.get_stock (stock/api.py:5), but the only caller, sync() in stock/jobs.py:12, still passes only sku. Every call raises TypeError, so the nightly sync fails on its first SKU and produces no output.
integration_findings.suggested_fix: Thread a warehouse argument through sync(), e.g. def sync(skus: list[str], warehouse: str) -> list[dict] and call api.get_stock(sku, warehouse). Update the sync() callers to pass the warehouse as well.

integration_findings.detected_pattern: sku and warehouse passed unvalidated from HTTP-facing get_stock into repository.fetch f-string SQL
integration_findings.issue: api.py is documented as HTTP-facing, and get_stock forwards sku and warehouse unchanged to repository.fetch, where repository.py:11 interpolates both into an f-string SQL query. Request-supplied values can therefore inject SQL. The f-string itself is covered by the single-file pass; this finding is the cross-module data flow that makes it reachable. The HTTP route that calls get_stock is not in the PR's changed files, so reachability depends on that route passing request input through.
integration_findings.suggested_fix: Parameterise the query in stock/repository.py:11 (cursor.execute('SELECT qty FROM stock WHERE sku = %s AND warehouse = %s', (sku, warehouse))) and validate sku and warehouse at the API boundary in get_stock before calling the repository.

proposed.scenario: A list holding one item totals that item's qty rather than 0; this fails on the PR 418 loop that starts at index 1.
Totalling the empty_stock fixture returns 0, guarding the changed loop bounds.
With the same SKU stocked in north and south, fetch('A1', 'south') returns south's qty and not north's, using a fake cursor that filters rows by warehouse.
A SKU containing an apostrophe (e.g. O'Neil-1) returns its own row from an in-memory sqlite stock table instead of raising a SQL error, which the f-string query on PR 418 line 11 would cause.
A SKU with no row in the requested warehouse returns qty 0 for that warehouse.
get_stock('A1', 'south') returns south's quantity when the SKU is also stocked in north, in tests/test_api.py.

sync(['A1', 'B2']) returns one stock entry per SKU without raising; this fails today with TypeError because jobs.py line 12 calls api.get_stock without the warehouse argument, in tests/test_jobs.py with the database stubbed.

skipped_as_duplicate.scenario: total_qty counts every item in the list (the PR 418 loop skips items[0]; this existing test currently fails with 9 instead of 12, so it is the regression guard).
fetch returns the qty for a known SKU.
